Clipshot needs to see new screenshots to copy them. Choose \"Allow all\": it never reads anything else, and it has no internet access.

No internet permission. No account. No tracking.\nNothing ever leaves your phone.
One minute after the copy, the screenshot is deleted from your photos. It stays on the clipboard.
Waiting for \"All files access\", which is off. Turn it on in Permissions; Clipshot uses it for this one thing.
No account. No tracking. No ads.
Nothing leaves your device unless you choose it.
The code is open, so anyone can check this.
Internal review. No external audit yet.
No app on this phone can open this link.
Resets Clipshot to how it was on first launch.
Your settings, counters and the last three copies are deleted, and \"Remove from gallery\" is turned off. Your screenshots in the gallery are not touched.
Nothing. This app has no internet access.
When you paste, the app you paste into gets that screenshot. Nothing else is shared.
The optional accessibility service cannot read your screen. It receives no events and only presses the screenshot button.
Clipshot\'s data is excluded from cloud backups and phone-to-phone transfers.
Links in About open in your browser or mail app, only when you tap them. Clipshot itself never connects to anything.
Each one is for one feature. Turn any of them off whenever you like: Clipshot adapts the next time you open it.
To see each new screenshot and copy it to the clipboard. This is what Clipshot does.
Screenshots are not copied for now. Allow it again to pick up where you left off.
Only for \"Remove from gallery\": it deletes the screenshot from your photos one minute after the copy.
\"Remove from gallery\" is on but can\'t delete anything until this is on. Your screenshots stay in your photos.
Not needed while \"Remove from gallery\" is off.
Only for Capture: the tile and the accessibility button press the screenshot button. It can\'t read your screen.
Capture is off. The two buttons still work, and still copy.
Clipshot also starts again after your phone restarts, so it keeps working. Android allows this at install and has no switch for it.
Take a screenshot from Quick Settings or the accessibility button.
Android only lets apps take a screenshot through an accessibility service. Clipshot\'s service can\'t read your screen; it only presses the screenshot button.
In the accessibility settings, open Clipshot and turn it on.
If Android says the setting is restricted: App info, menu ⋮, Allow restricted settings.
Tap the Capture tile in Quick Settings, or the accessibility button. The screenshot goes to the clipboard.
Screenshot from a tile or the accessibility button

Takes a screenshot when you tap the Capture tile or the accessibility button, so Clipshot can copy it to the clipboard. This service receives no events and can\'t read what is on your screen. Its only action is pressing the screenshot button. Clipshot has no internet access.
